To left-align table captions without the `caption` package, you need to modify LaTeX's internal `\@makecaption` command, which controls how captions are formatted in standard document classes (`article`, `report`, `book`).

### 🔧 Preamble Code
Add this to your preamble:
```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}% ← Removed left \hfil to left-align
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

### 📖 How It Works
- LaTeX centers short captions using `\hb@xt@\hsize{\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil}`. Removing the left `\hfil` pushes the caption box to the left margin.
- Multi-line captions (`#1: #2\par`) are already left-aligned (justified by default). The code above preserves this behavior.
- `\makeatletter`/`\makeatother` are required because `@` is used in internal LaTeX command names.

### 📝 Minimal Working Example
```latex
\documentclass{article}

\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[ht]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{cc}
    A & B \\
    1 & 2 \\
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{This short caption is now left-aligned.}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[ht]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{cc}
    A & B \\
    3 & 4 \\
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{This is a much longer caption that spans multiple lines to demonstrate that multi-line captions remain properly formatted and left-aligned as well.}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

### 🔍 Optional: Ragged-Right Multi-line Captions
If you want multi-line captions to be strictly left-aligned (ragged-right, not justified), change the multi-line branch like this:
```latex
\ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
  \raggedright #1: #2\par
\else
```

### ⚠️ Important Notes
- This works for standard classes (`article`, `report`, `book`). 
- If you use **KOMA-Script** (`scrartcl`, etc.), use its built-in system instead:
  ```latex
  \addtokomafont{caption}{\raggedright}
  \setcapindent{0pt}
  ```
- If you use **memoir**, it has its own caption formatting hooks (`\captionstyle`, `\captionnamefont`, etc.).
- Redefining `\@makecaption` may conflict with other packages that modify captions (e.g., `subfig`, `floatrow`). Load those packages *before* this redefinition if needed.

To left-align table captions without the `caption` package, you need to modify LaTeX's internal `\@makecaption` command, which controls how captions are formatted in standard document classes (`article`, `report`, `book`).

### 🔧 Preamble Code
Add this to your preamble:
```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}% ← Removed left \hfil to left-align
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

### 📖 How It Works
- LaTeX centers short captions using `\hb@xt@\hsize{\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil}`. Removing the left `\hfil` pushes the caption box to the left margin.
- Multi-line captions (`#1: #2\par`) are already left-aligned (justified by default). The code above preserves this behavior.
- `\makeatletter`/`\makeatother` are required because `@` is used in internal LaTeX command names.

### 📝 Minimal Working Example
```latex
\documentclass{article}

\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global \@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[ht]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{cc}
    A & B \\
    1 & 2 \\
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{This short caption is now left-aligned.}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[ht]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{cc}
    A & B \\
    3 & 4 \\
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{This is a much longer caption that spans multiple lines to demonstrate that multi-line captions remain properly formatted and left-aligned as well.}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

### 🔍 Optional: Ragged-Right Multi-line Captions
If you want multi-line captions to be strictly left-aligned (ragged-right, not justified), change the multi-line branch like this:
```latex
\ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
  \raggedright #1: #2\par
\else
```

### ⚠️ Important Notes
- This works for standard classes (`article`, `report`, `book`). 
- If you use **KOMA-Script** (`scrartcl`, etc.), use its built-in system instead:
  ```latex
  \addtokomafont{caption}{\raggedright}
  \setcapindent{0pt}
  ```
- If you use **memoir**, it has its own caption formatting hooks (`\captionstyle`, `\captionnamefont`, etc.).
- Redefining `\@makecaption` may conflict with other packages that modify captions (e.g., `subfig`, `floatrow`). Load those packages *before* this redefinition if needed.
